items.name: ScanDot
items.description: Experimental Android 3D scanning and point-cloud viewer
items.readme:
# ScanDot

[![CI](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

ScanDot is an experimental Android app for capturing and viewing 3D point clouds on a supported phone. It combines ARCore camera tracking and depth estimates, saves scans locally, and provides an interactive viewer.

The repository also contains a separate video photogrammetry pipeline that runs on a workstation using FFmpeg and COLMAP. **The Android app does not reconstruct ordinary video with photogrammetry on the phone.**

## Current status

- Capture, save and reopen point clouds on devices that support ARCore Depth.
- Rotate, pan and zoom scans in the viewer. An optional full-depth mode interpolates missing depth and can distort surfaces.
- Prepare video frames and run a sparse or dense COLMAP reconstruction on a workstation.

This is an early prototype. Results can contain gaps, drift and noise; they are not textured meshes or validated measurements. Reflective, transparent and textureless subjects are difficult. Capture quality and device compatibility need further testing.

## Try the preview

Download the [preview APK](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/releases/tag/v0.3.0-preview.1). The release notes describe compatibility and signing limitations.

## Build the Android app

You need JDK 17, Android SDK 36, and an Android device with ARCore Depth support. Camera permission is required; Google Play Services for AR may require installation or an update.

```sh
cd android-app
./gradlew assembleDebug lintDebug testDebugUnitTest
```

On Windows, use `gradlew.bat` in place of `./gradlew`. The debug APK is written to `android-app/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. Install it as an update to preserve existing app data.

In the app, name the scan, tap **Start scan**, and move slowly around the subject in good light. Save it, then open it from **Results**. Scans are stored in the app's private storage; uninstalling the app removes them.

## Workstation video pipeline

The benchmark requires Python 3.12 or newer, FFmpeg, FFprobe and a compatible COLMAP installation. Dense reconstruction requires a compatible COLMAP configuration. From the repository root:

```sh
python -m processing.benchmark prepare "path/to/input.mp4" --output "path/to/new-run" --fps 5
python -m processing.benchmark reconstruct "path/to/new-run" --colmap "path/to/colmap" --dense
```

The output directory must not already exist. Omit `--dense` for a sparse-only run. See the subcommand `--help` output for options. A successful run does not establish complete or accurate geometry.

The Python tests use the standard library:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Project structure

```text
android-app/  Android capture, local storage and point-cloud viewer
processing/   Video preparation and COLMAP orchestration
tests/        Python tests with synthetic fixtures
tools/        Workstation utilities
```

CI runs the Android build, lint and JVM tests, plus the Python unit tests. It does not exercise a camera, ARCore tracking, GPU reconstruction or measurement accuracy.

See the [wiki](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/wiki) for installation, capture and troubleshooting guides. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development checks and [LICENSE](LICENSE) for reuse terms.

items.name: kraken-mount
items.description: Minimalist PS5 game mounter supporting PKG, folder dumps, lz4, and zstd
items.readme: A PS5 ELF payload. It finds games on the internal SSD and on USB or extended drives. It mounts debug FPKG `.pkg` files, game folders (plain, or packed with zstd or LZ4). ## How to 1. [ampr-emu-ng](https://github.com/quer3q/ampr-emu-ng) comes bundled and is installed into `/data/krakenmount/ampr/` at start. To run another build, put its `libSceAmpr.sprx` there; it is kept until you delete it. 2. Put each game in a scan root: `/data/homebrew`, `/data/etaHEN/games`, or `homebrew`, `etaHEN/games` or the root of a USB drive. A `.pkg` must be a plaintext debug FPKG from dump-forge. A folder needs `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/param.json`. Backports go in `/backports/*`. 3. Download `kraken-mount.elf` from [Releases](https://github.com/quer3q/kraken-mount/releases) and send it once to the ELF loader (elfldr, port 9021): `nc -w 3 9021 < kraken-mount.elf`. It saves a copy on the console, and from then on the Kraken Mount tile on the home screen starts it (elfldr must be running). 4. Each game gets a " registered" notification and its own home-screen tile. 5. Open the Kraken Mount tile, or `http://:8097/` from a computer, to see the games, rebuild or delete them, change settings and read the log. Caches live in `/data/krakenmount/caches/`, settings in `/data/krakenmount/config.toml` and the log in `/data/krakenmount/kraken.log`. To build it yourself: `ps5/build.sh` (needs Docker), output `target/ps5/kraken-mount.elf`. ## Thanks - [drakmor/ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus): home-screen registration, the fakelib sandbox overlay and backports are ported from it. - [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): the PS5 toolchain. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). Third-party notices are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`.

items.name: islandcn
items.description: The open-source Dynamic Island for React, installed with shadcn.
items.readme: # islandcn A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://islandcn.dev/r/island-core.json ``` ```tsx "use client"; import { Island, IslandProvider, useIsland } from "@/lib/island"; // Mount once near the root. ; // Then, from any component inside it: const island = useIsland(); const upload = island.start({ id: "upload", label: "Uploading report.pdf", compact: { leading: , trailing: }, expanded: { center: report.pdf, bottom: }, }); upload.update({ compact: { trailing: } }); upload.end(); ``` ## What's here - **The engine** (`lib/island/`, registry item `island-core`): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only. - **Presets** (`components/islandcn/`): upload, timer, now playing, incoming call, ride or delivery ETA, recording, nearby transfer, battery and the split, each one file on the engine, plus the content kit they share. - **The playground** (`/playground`): build an island for your app from a preset or a blank activity, fire every action, tune the motion and copy the install command and the code. - **The site and docs** (`app/`, `docs/content/`). Coding agents can use the optional `islandcn-skill` registry item as an install helper; see `/docs/agent-skill`. ## Develop ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev # http://localhost:3000 pnpm typecheck pnpm build # builds the registry into public/r, then the site ``` Read `AGENTS.md` before changing anything. The recordings the motion was fitted to are not in this repo. `/lab` still plays every transition from its built-in sequences in `pnpm dev`; `/compare`, which sets the web side against the recordings, has nothing to show, and the one test that reads them is skipped. ## License MIT, copyright (c) 2026 Leo. See `LICENSE`. islandcn copies the look and motion of Apple's island, but none of Apple's assets. It is not affiliated with Apple. Dynamic Island is a trademark of Apple Inc.

## What Is Manus

Manus is an autonomous AI agent designed to run code and control a browser on your behalf. Instead of acting like a simple chatbot that only answers questions, Manus AI agent takes action. It can write and execute scripts, open web pages, interact with elements, and carry out multi-step tasks with minimal supervision. This makes Manus code automation useful for anyone who wants to reduce manual effort without learning a full programming stack.

The core idea behind Manus browser control is practical freedom. You describe what you need, and the agent figures out the steps. Whether that means checking a website for updated information, filling out a repetitive form, or testing a small script, Manus autonomous tasks turn your instructions into completed actions. Manus personal assistant works quietly in the background, ready whenever you need to delegate a small but annoying job.

Manus is not a heavy studio suite or a complex enterprise platform. It is a focused helper built for home, study, and small tasks. Students can use Manus code automation to organize research notes or run quick calculations. Remote workers can rely on Manus browser control to gather data from multiple pages. Anyone juggling several small projects can let Manus autonomous tasks handle the repetitive parts while they focus on the parts that need human judgment.

Over longer sessions, Manus personal assistant proves its value through consistency. You do not need to re-explain the same workflow every time. Manus AI agent remembers the pattern and applies it again. Manus code automation and Manus browser control work together so that a task starting in a script can finish in a browser, or the other way around.
